$comment: Tombstone ledger. KEYED BY X STATUS ID and by nothing else.
A removal is executed by DELETING the whole record from prompts.json — including its
prompt field, not a flag and not a render-time filter — appending a tombstone here, and
running `node scripts/build.mjs --restamp`.
Why the status id: our slug is derived from an editable upstream title and the sourceUrl is
usually the thing being corrected, so either would stop matching and the row would come back
on the next refresh from upstream. The status id never moves.
One status id can match MORE THAN ONE row, because a single post sometimes published several
distinct prompts. A tombstone removes all of them. That is intended: the request is about the
post. If a rights holder asks for one row of such a post and not the others, say so on the
issue — that case needs a human, not a different key.
Entry shape — {
"statusId":   string, digits only, REQUIRED. Matches prompts[].statusId.
"removed_at": string, "YYYY-MM-DD", REQUIRED.
"basis":      string, REQUIRED. e.g. "author request", "rights holder request",
"trademark", "privacy".
"issue":      integer, OPTIONAL. Omit when the request arrived by email.
Never record prompt text here, and never record who asked: not a handle, not a name, not the
fact that a particular person objected. A public list of people who objected is the remedy
creating the harm.
The build treats this file as a FILTER first and an assertion second: a tombstoned status id
is dropped before selection, then asserted absent from the output. Ledger and corpus are
checked against each other on every run, so a tombstone whose row is still published fails.
